name: Anamorelin
description: An oral ghrelin receptor agonist that stimulates GH and IGF-1 release, used to treat cachexia, anorexia, and muscle wasting in cancer patients.
storageInfo: Store at room temperature in a dry container.
mechanismOfAction: Oral ghrelin receptor agonist that stimulates GH and IGF-1 release and increases appetite signaling for cancer cachexia.
researchEvidence: Phase III Clinical Trial (Approved in Japan)

name: CJC-1295 (no DAC)
description: Also known as Mod GRF 1-29, a short-acting Growth Hormone Releasing Hormone (GHRH) analog that mimics physiological growth hormone pulses when paired with a GHRP.
storageInfo: Store reconstituted vial in refrigerator; sensitive to mechanical agitation.
mechanismOfAction: Modified GRF (1-29) analog that mimics natural GHRH pulses, binding to GHRH receptors on somatotroph cells to stimulate GH secretion.

name: CJC-1295 (with DAC)
description: Growth Hormone Releasing Hormone (GHRH) analog with Drug Affinity Complex (DAC) which binds to plasma albumin, extending its activity to stimulate growth hormone release over several days.
storageInfo: Refrigerate reconstituted vial (2-8°C) and use within 28 days.
mechanismOfAction: GHRH analog with Drug Affinity Complex (DAC) that binds albumin for extended activity, stimulating pulsatile GH release from the anterior pituitary.

name: Capromorelin
description: An oral growth hormone secretagogue that increases GH levels and appetite. Extensively studied in veterinary medicine and clinical research.
storageInfo: Store at room temperature in a dark container.
mechanismOfAction: Oral ghrelin receptor agonist that increases GH levels and appetite, extensively studied in veterinary medicine.

name: Follistatin 344
description: A synthetic isoform of follistatin, a naturally occurring glycoprotein that acts as a potent inhibitor of myostatin and activin. By binding and neutralizing myostatin (the primary negative regulator of muscle growth), follistatin 344 removes the brake on muscle development, potentially allowing for increased hypertrophy.
storageInfo: Store reconstituted solution at 2-8°C. Sensitive to agitation — do not shake.
mechanismOfAction: Acts as a ligand trap for TGF-β superfamily members, primarily myostatin and activin A. Binding neutralizes their negative regulatory effect on skeletal muscle, allowing increased muscle protein synthesis and satellite cell activation.
legalStatus: Research Chemical / WADA Banned (Gene doping category)
researchEvidence: Phase I Clinical Trial (Gene therapy for muscular dystrophy)

name: GHRP-2 (Pralmorelin)
description: Growth Hormone Releasing Peptide-2 is a synthetic ghrelin agonist that acts on the hypothalamus and pituitary to stimulate growth hormone release, with moderate appetite stimulation. Also marketed as a diagnostic agent (Pralmorelin) in Japan for evaluating pituitary GH secretion.
storageInfo: Keep reconstituted solution in refrigerator. Protect from mechanical shock.
sideEffects: temporary rise in prolactin and cortisol at high doses
mechanismOfAction: Synthetic hexapeptide ghrelin receptor agonist that acts on hypothalamus and pituitary to stimulate GH release with moderate appetite stimulation.

name: GHRP-6
description: Growth Hormone Releasing Peptide-6 stimulates growth hormone secretion and induces a significant appetite increase via activation of the ghrelin receptor.
storageInfo: Refrigerate (2-8°C) after reconstitution. Stable up to 28 days.
mechanismOfAction: Synthetic hexapeptide ghrelin receptor agonist that stimulates GH secretion and significantly increases appetite via ghrelin pathway activation.

name: Hexarelin
description: A potent synthetic hexapeptide GHRP that stimulates growth hormone release while showing cardioprotective properties. It has a high resistance to enzymatic degradation. Examorelin is the International Nonproprietary Name (INN) for Hexarelin.
sideEffects: mild increase in cortisol and prolactin
mechanismOfAction: Potent synthetic hexapeptide GHRP that stimulates GH release via ghrelin receptor agonism, with additional cardioprotective properties through CD36 receptor interaction.

name: IGF-1 DES (1-3)
description: A truncated analog of IGF-1 lacking the first three N-terminal amino acids. This modification reduces IGFBP affinity by over 100-fold, making it approximately 10 times more potent than native IGF-1 at the receptor level. Very short half-life makes it primarily a locally-acting agent.
storageInfo: Store reconstituted solution at 2-8°C. Use within 24 hours.
mechanismOfAction: N-terminal truncation eliminates IGFBP binding, allowing direct IGF-1R activation at injection site. Activates PI3K/Akt/mTOR for localized protein synthesis, satellite cell activation, and amino acid uptake with minimal systemic effects.

name: IGF-1 LR3
description: Long R3 Insulin-Like Growth Factor-1 is a synthetic 83-amino acid analog of human IGF-1 with an arginine substitution at position 3 and a 13-amino acid N-terminal extension. These modifications reduce IGFBP binding, resulting in a dramatically extended half-life (~20-30 hours vs. 12-15 minutes for native IGF-1) and higher bioavailability.
storageInfo: Store reconstituted solution at 2-8°C. Avoid repeated freeze-thaw cycles.
mechanismOfAction: Binds IGF-1 receptor with high affinity (reduced IGFBP sequestration), activating PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling cascade for protein synthesis, satellite cell activation, amino acid uptake, and anti-apoptotic effects.

name: Ipamorelin
description: A selective Growth Hormone Releasing Peptide (GHRP) agonist of the ghrelin receptor. Stimulates GH secretion without increasing appetite, cortisol, or prolactin.
storageInfo: Store in refrigerator (2-8°C) after reconstitution. Use within 28 days.
mechanismOfAction: Selective ghrelin receptor (GHSR) agonist that stimulates GH release without significantly affecting cortisol, prolactin, or appetite.

name: MK-677 (Ibutamoren)
description: An orally active, non-peptide ghrelin receptor agonist that mimics the growth hormone-stimulating action of ghrelin. Promotes fat-free mass and bone mineral density.
storageInfo: Store in a cool, dry place at room temperature in a sealed container.
mechanismOfAction: Non-peptide oral ghrelin receptor agonist that mimics ghrelin signaling to increase GH and IGF-1 levels.

name: Macimorelin
description: An FDA-approved oral ghrelin agonist used as a diagnostic agent to detect adult growth hormone deficiency.
storageInfo: Store lyophilized powder at room temperature. Reconstitute immediately before use.
contraindications: Concomitant use of drugs known to prolong QT interval
mechanismOfAction: Oral ghrelin receptor agonist used diagnostically to stimulate GH release for detection of adult GH deficiency.

name: Sermorelin
description: A Growth Hormone Releasing Hormone (GHRH) fragment consisting of the first 29 amino acids. Promotes natural GH production by the pituitary gland. Indirectly supports sexual drive and energy profiles via increased natural GH levels.
storageInfo: Refrigerate reconstituted solution. Protect from direct light.
mechanismOfAction: GHRH fragment (1-29) that binds GHRH receptors on pituitary somatotrophs, promoting natural pulsatile GH production.

name: Tabimorelin
description: An orally active growth hormone secretagogue which acts on ghrelin receptors to stimulate systemic GH release in clinical trials.
storageInfo: Store at room temperature in a dry environment.
mechanismOfAction: Oral GH secretagogue acting via ghrelin receptor agonism to stimulate systemic GH release.

name: Tesamorelin
description: An FDA-approved Growth Hormone Releasing Hormone (GHRH) analog indicated for reducing excess abdominal fat in HIV-infected patients with lipodystrophy.
storageInfo: Store in refrigerator. Protect reconstituted solution from light.
mechanismOfAction: GHRH analog that stimulates pituitary GH release, reducing visceral adipose tissue in HIV-associated lipodystrophy.

name: ARA-290 (Cibinetide)
description: A synthetic peptide modeled from erythropoietin (EPO) structure that targets the innate repair receptor to reduce pain and promote tissue healing in neuropathy.
storageInfo: Store reconstituted solution at 2-8°C. Protect from light.
mechanismOfAction: EPO-derived peptide that activates the innate repair receptor (heterodimer of EPOR and CD131), promoting tissue healing and reducing neuropathic pain.

name: Ac-SDKP
description: A naturally occurring tetrapeptide that inhibits cardiac fibrosis, promotes angiogenesis, and modulates inflammation in cardiovascular tissues.
contraindications: Co-administration with ACE inhibitors (can spike peptide levels)
mechanismOfAction: Endogenous tetrapeptide that inhibits cardiac fibrosis by blocking TGF-β/Smad signaling and promotes angiogenesis via VEGF pathway activation.

name: BPC-157
description: Body Protection Compound-157 is a synthetic peptide derived from human gastric juice. Preclinical trials show it accelerates tendon, ligament, muscle, and gut healing.
storageInfo: Store reconstituted vial in refrigerator (2-8°C). Lyophilized powder in freezer.
mechanismOfAction: Gastric pentadecapeptide that activates VEGFR2, FAK-paxillin, and ERK1/2 pathways promoting angiogenesis, tendon/ligament repair, and anti-inflammatory signaling. Modulates the nitric oxide system.

name: BPC-157 Arginate (Stable)
description: A salt-stabilized form of BPC-157 using L-Arginine. Resistant to gastric acid degradation, making it highly effective for oral administration.
storageInfo: Store in dry place at room temperature. Highly stable.
mechanismOfAction: L-Arginine salt form of BPC-157 with enhanced gastric acid resistance, maintaining the same VEGFR2/FAK/ERK signaling cascade as standard BPC-157.

name: Chondrogenesis Peptide (Cartilage)
description: A peptide derived from growth factor structures that stimulates cartilage matrix synthesis and chondrocyte differentiation.
mechanismOfAction: Growth factor-derived peptide that stimulates SOX9 and type II collagen expression in chondrocytes, promoting cartilage matrix synthesis.

name: Glutamine Peptide (Gut Recovery)
description: Peptide-bound glutamine offering superior absorption for mucosal repair in inflammatory bowel conditions.
mechanismOfAction: Peptide-bound glutamine that provides superior absorption for mucosal repair by serving as primary fuel for enterocytes and supporting tight junction integrity.

name: KPV
description: A tripeptide (Lys-Pro-Val) derived from alpha-MSH. Acts as a potent anti-inflammatory agent, especially in gastrointestinal inflammatory disorders and skin healing.
storageInfo: Refrigerate reconstituted vials. Stable topically at room temp.
mechanismOfAction: C-terminal tripeptide of alpha-MSH that inhibits NF-κB signaling and pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α) without melanocortin receptor binding.

name: Larazotide Acetate (AT-1001)
description: A tight junction regulator peptide studied for celiac disease. Helps repair the intestinal mucosal barrier and prevent leaky gut syndrome.
storageInfo: Store at room temperature in a dry container.
mechanismOfAction: Tight junction regulator that prevents zonulin-mediated intestinal permeability increase, restoring epithelial barrier integrity.

name: Osteogenic Peptide (Bone Healing)
description: Synthetic peptide that mimics bone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs) to stimulate osteoblast activity and bone healing.
contraindications: History of osteosarcoma or bone oncology
mechanismOfAction: BMP-mimetic peptide that activates Smad 1/5/8 signaling cascade, stimulating osteoblast differentiation and bone matrix deposition.

name: PEA Peptide (Anti-Inflammatory)
description: Endogenous fatty acid amide acting as a lipid messenger peptide to modulate localized neuroinflammation and pain pathways.
mechanismOfAction: Endogenous fatty acid amide that activates PPARα nuclear receptors and indirectly enhances endocannabinoid tone, modulating neuroinflammation and pain.

name: TB-500
description: Synthetic peptide containing the active healing domain of Thymosin Beta-4. Promotes blood vessel growth, tissue repair, and cell migration in musculoskeletal injuries.
storageInfo: Refrigerate reconstituted solution (2-8°C). Keep protected from light.
mechanismOfAction: Synthetic fragment of Thymosin Beta-4 that promotes actin polymerization, cell migration, blood vessel growth, and tissue repair via upregulation of cell-building proteins.

name: TB4 Frag (1-4) (Ac-SDKP)
description: The amino-terminal fragment of Thymosin Beta-4 that regulates inflammation, angiogenesis, and collagen deposition.
mechanismOfAction: N-terminal fragment (Ac-SDKP) of Thymosin Beta-4 that regulates inflammation, inhibits collagen deposition, and promotes angiogenesis.

name: Thymosin Beta-4 (Full Length)
description: The full 43-amino-acid peptide that occurs naturally in human tissues. Essential for cell migration, wound repair, and muscle fiber regeneration.
storageInfo: Keep reconstituted vial refrigerated. Protect from light.
mechanismOfAction: Full 43-amino-acid thymosin beta-4 peptide that sequesters G-actin monomers, promoting cell migration, wound repair, and anti-inflammatory responses.

name: Vasoactive Intestinal Peptide (VIP)
description: A neuromodulator peptide that regulates inflammatory responses, lung tissue healing, and blood flow, often used in Chronic Inflammatory Response Syndrome (CIRS).
mechanismOfAction: 28-amino-acid neuropeptide that binds VPAC1/VPAC2 receptors, regulating vasodilation, anti-inflammatory cytokine release, and bronchodilation.
legalStatus: Research Chemical / FDA-Approved (Aviptadil for CIRS protocol)

name: 5-Amino-1Q
description: A small-molecule inhibitor of NNMT (nicotinamide N-methyltransferase). Promotes fat cell metabolism, muscle preservation, and energy expenditure.
storageInfo: Store at room temperature in a dry container.
mechanismOfAction: Small-molecule inhibitor of nicotinamide N-methyltransferase (NNMT), promoting SAM-dependent fat metabolism and energy expenditure.

name: AOD-9604
description: Anti-Obesity Drug-9604 is a synthetic C-terminal fragment of human Growth Hormone (hGH 177-191). Promotes lipolysis (fat breakdown) and inhibits lipogenesis without elevating blood glucose.
mechanismOfAction: C-terminal fragment of hGH (177-191) that stimulates lipolysis via beta-3 adrenergic receptors and inhibits lipogenesis without affecting blood glucose or IGF-1.
researchEvidence: Phase IIb Clinical Trial (Did not advance)

name: Cagrilintide (Amylin Analog)
description: A long-acting amylin receptor agonist that works synergistically with GLP-1 agonists to enhance satiety and delay gastric emptying.
typicalDoseRange: 0.3 mg - 2.4 mg weekly (typically co-administered with Semaglutide)
mechanismOfAction: Long-acting amylin receptor agonist that enhances satiety signaling and delays gastric emptying via area postrema and vagal afferent pathways.

name: Dulaglutide
description: An FDA-approved weekly GLP-1 receptor agonist (Trulicity) for glycemic control and cardiovascular risk reduction.
mechanismOfAction: Weekly GLP-1 receptor agonist fused to an Fc fragment for extended half-life, providing sustained incretin signaling for glycemic control.

name: Exenatide (Byetta/Bydureon)
description: The first GLP-1 receptor agonist approved by the FDA, derived from Gila monster saliva, available in daily or weekly formulas.
mechanismOfAction: GLP-1 receptor agonist derived from exendin-4 (Gila monster venom) that stimulates glucose-dependent insulin secretion.

name: HGH Fragment 177-191
description: The lipolytic fragment of human growth hormone that promotes fat burning without affect blood glucose levels.
mechanismOfAction: C-terminal fragment of human growth hormone that activates lipolytic pathways via beta-3 adrenergic receptors without affecting blood glucose.

name: Liraglutide
description: An FDA-approved daily GLP-1 receptor agonist for weight management (Saxenda) and type 2 diabetes (Victoza).
storageInfo: Refrigerate unused pens. Keep in-use pens up to 30 days at room temp.
mechanismOfAction: Daily GLP-1 receptor agonist with acylation for albumin binding, prolonging half-life and providing sustained incretin-mediated glucose control.

name: Lixisenatide
description: A short-acting daily GLP-1 receptor agonist focused on postprandial glucose control.
mechanismOfAction: Short-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist focused on postprandial glucose control via delayed gastric emptying.

name: Mazdutide (GLP1-GCGR)
description: A dual GLP-1 and glucagon receptor agonist showing potent fat reduction and lipid profile improvement.
mechanismOfAction: Dual GLP-1 and glucagon receptor agonist that combines incretin-mediated appetite suppression with glucagon-driven hepatic fat oxidation.

name: Orforglipron
description: An investigational oral, non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonist providing weight loss without the need for weekly injections.
mechanismOfAction: Oral non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonist with small-molecule structure enabling oral bioavailability without injection.

name: Retatrutide (Triple Agonist)
description: An investigational triple receptor agonist targeting GLP-1, GIP, and Glucagon receptors, exhibiting substantial weight loss outcomes in Phase II trials.
mechanismOfAction: Triple agonist targeting GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon receptors simultaneously for synergistic effects on appetite, glucose metabolism, and fat oxidation.

name: Semaglutide
description: An FDA-approved GLP-1 receptor agonist that regulates blood sugar, slows stomach emptying, and reduces hunger to assist in weight loss.
storageInfo: Store in refrigerator (2-8°C). Protect from heat and direct sunlight.
mechanismOfAction: Long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist that mimics incretin signaling to reduce appetite, slow gastric emptying, and enhance insulin secretion.

name: Tesofensine
description: A monoamine reuptake inhibitor that suppresses appetite and increases energy expenditure. Demonstrates significant weight loss in clinical studies.
mechanismOfAction: Triple monoamine reuptake inhibitor (serotonin, norepinephrine, dopamine) that suppresses appetite centrally and increases basal metabolic rate.

name: Tirzepatide
description: An FDA-approved dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist that offers high efficacy in blood sugar control and body weight reduction.
mechanismOfAction: Dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist that provides synergistic incretin signaling for enhanced glucose control and weight reduction.

name: Humanin
description: A 24-amino acid mitochondrial-derived peptide (MDP) encoded by the mitochondrial 16S rRNA gene. First discovered in 2001 in brain regions spared from Alzheimer's disease. Demonstrates potent anti-apoptotic, neuroprotective, and cytoprotective properties. Circulating levels decline with age.
storageInfo: Store reconstituted solution at 2-8°C. Highly sensitive to degradation.
mechanismOfAction: Binds and inhibits pro-apoptotic Bax protein, preventing mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization. Activates STAT3, ERK1/2, and PI3K/Akt survival signaling pathways. Interacts with IGFBP-3 and enhances insulin sensitivity.
researchEvidence: Preclinical Only (Extensive animal and in-vitro studies)

name: MOTS-c
description: A mitochondrial-derived peptide (MDP) encoded by the mitochondrial 12S rRNA gene. Regulates metabolic homeostasis by activating AMPK signaling, increasing insulin sensitivity, promoting exercise capacity, and enhancing fatty acid oxidation. Primarily studied for its role in longevity and metabolic health.
mechanismOfAction: Mitochondrial-derived peptide that activates AMPK signaling, improving insulin sensitivity, glucose uptake, and fatty acid oxidation.

name: SS-31 (Elamipretide)
description: A synthetic mitochondria-targeted tetrapeptide (D-Arg-Dmt-Lys-Phe-NH2) that selectively binds cardiolipin in the inner mitochondrial membrane. FDA-approved as FORZINITY™ (September 2025) for Barth syndrome, making it the first approved mitochondria-targeted therapeutic. Improves mitochondrial efficiency, reduces oxidative stress, and enhances ATP production.
storageInfo: Store in refrigerator (2-8°C). Protect from light.
mechanismOfAction: Selectively binds to cardiolipin on the inner mitochondrial membrane, stabilizing cytochrome c interaction and optimizing electron transport chain efficiency. Reduces reactive oxygen species production and prevents cardiolipin peroxidation.

name: Cerebrolysin
description: A peptide mixture purified from pig brain tissue, rich in neurotrophic factors. Used for stroke recovery, dementia, and traumatic brain injury.
storageInfo: Store in cool space. Ampoules are single-use; discard remainder.
mechanismOfAction: Mixture of neurotrophic peptides that mimic BDNF, GDNF, and CNTF signaling to promote neuronal survival, synaptogenesis, and neuroplasticity.
researchEvidence: Phase III Clinical Trial (Approved outside US)

name: Cortagen
description: A synthetic bioregulatory peptide (Ala-Glu-Asp-Pro) acting specifically on cerebral cortex cells to reduce age-related cognitive decline.
mechanismOfAction: Synthetic bioregulatory tetrapeptide (Ala-Glu-Asp-Pro) that acts specifically on cerebral cortex cells via gene expression modulation.

name: DSIP (Delta Sleep-Inducing Peptide)
description: A naturally occurring nonapeptide (Trp-Ala-Gly-Gly-Asp-Ala-Ser-Gly-Glu) first isolated from rabbit brain in 1977. Proposed to promote delta wave (slow-wave) sleep and regulate circadian rhythms. Historical evidence is mixed — some studies show modest sleep improvements while others show no significant difference from placebo.
storageInfo: Store reconstituted solution at 2-8°C. Extremely fragile — use within 14 days.
mechanismOfAction: Modulates GABAergic transmission, interacts with opioid receptors, and regulates the HPA axis to reduce cortisol. May promote slow-wave sleep via serotonin pathway modulation. Exact mechanism remains unclear.

name: Dihexa
description: An oligopeptide drug candidate derived from angiotensin IV that binds to HGF, exhibiting potent neurogenic and memory-enhancing capabilities in laboratory models. Also promotes tissue recovery and angiogenesis via its HGF binding activity.
contraindications: Active cancer (due to HGF pathway stimulation)
mechanismOfAction: Angiotensin IV-derived hexapeptide that potentiates hepatocyte growth factor (HGF) signaling via c-Met receptor, promoting neurogenesis, synaptogenesis, and tissue repair.

name: FGL Peptide
description: A peptide derived from neural cell adhesion molecule (NCAM) that activates the FGF receptor to stimulate synapse formation and memory retention.
mechanismOfAction: NCAM-derived peptide that activates FGF receptor to stimulate synapse formation, LTP enhancement, and memory retention.

name: L-Glutamyl-L-Selenocysteine
description: A seleno-peptide functioning as a cellular antioxidant to protect neurons from oxidative stress.
mechanismOfAction: Seleno-peptide that functions as a glutathione peroxidase cofactor, protecting neurons from oxidative stress via selenium-dependent antioxidant mechanisms.

name: MIF-1
description: A naturally occurring tripeptide (Pro-Leu-Gly-NH2) that modulates dopamine receptors, studied for Parkinson's disease and depression symptoms.
mechanismOfAction: Naturally occurring tripeptide (Pro-Leu-Gly-NH2) that modulates dopamine D2 receptor sensitivity and opioid receptor interactions.

name: N-Acetyl Selank Amidate
description: A modified version of Selank designed to exhibit increased potency, biological activity, and half-life in the central nervous system.
mechanismOfAction: Acetylated and amidated Selank variant with increased CNS potency and prolonged biological half-life, enhancing anxiolytic and immunomodulatory effects.

name: N-Acetyl Semax Amidate
description: An acetylated and amidated variant of Semax providing increased blood-brain barrier penetration and enhanced stability.
mechanismOfAction: Acetylated and amidated Semax variant with increased BBB penetration and metabolic stability, enhancing BDNF expression more potently than standard Semax.

name: Noopept (GVS-111)
description: A proline-containing dipeptide designed to mimic the endogenous neuropeptide vasopressin. Enhances memory consolidation and learning capacity.
storageInfo: Store at room temperature in a dry container.
mechanismOfAction: Proline-containing dipeptide that enhances AMPA and NMDA receptor sensitivity, increases BDNF and NGF expression, and improves memory consolidation.

name: P21 Peptide
description: A synthetic peptide derived from CNTF (ciliary neurotrophic factor) that improves neurogenesis and synaptic plasticity.
mechanismOfAction: CNTF-derived peptide that promotes hippocampal neurogenesis via activation of STAT3 signaling and inhibition of LIF receptor.

name: PE-22-28
description: A synthetic heptapeptide ('mini-spadin') that selectively inhibits the TREK-1 (TWIK-related) potassium channel. Preclinical rodent studies show rapid antidepressant-like effects comparable to fluoxetine but with faster onset. Acts through serotonergic transmission modulation rather than sigma receptor pathways.
storageInfo: Store reconstituted solution at 2-8°C. Protect from light.
mechanismOfAction: Selective antagonist of the TREK-1 (KCNK2) two-pore domain potassium channel. Blocking TREK-1 increases neuronal excitability and facilitates serotonergic transmission, producing rapid antidepressant-like effects. Promotes BDNF expression and hippocampal neurogenesis.

name: Pinealon
description: A short bioregulator tripeptide (Glu-Asp-Arg) that protects brain tissues from hypoxia, improves memory, and coordinates circadian rhythms.
mechanismOfAction: Short bioregulator tripeptide (Glu-Asp-Arg) that protects brain tissues from hypoxia and normalizes circadian rhythms via pineal gland regulation.

name: RG14620 (EGF peptide)
description: An epidermal growth factor analog studied for cognitive support and neuronal survival in neurodegenerative models.
mechanismOfAction: EGF analog that supports neuronal survival through EGF receptor-mediated signaling in neurodegenerative models.

name: Selank
description: Synthetic anxiolytic peptide related to the immunomodulatory peptide Tuftsin, providing stress reduction and neurotransmitter balance without sedation. Also regulates IL-6 cytokine expression, acting as a bridge between nervous and immune systems.
storageInfo: Keep refrigerated. Stable at room temperature up to 7 days.
mechanismOfAction: Tuftsin analog that modulates GABA-ergic transmission, regulates IL-6 expression, and enhances enkephalin degradation enzyme inhibition for anxiolytic effects.

name: Semax
description: A synthetic heptapeptide derived from ACTH (4-7) with high neuroprotective, memory-enhancing, and stimulatory actions.
storageInfo: Store in refrigerator. Protect from direct light.
mechanismOfAction: Synthetic ACTH (4-7) analog that upregulates BDNF and NGF expression, enhances serotonergic and dopaminergic transmission, and provides neuroprotection.

name: Argireline (Acetyl Hexapeptide-8)
description: A peptide that mimics botulinum toxin mechanism by relaxing facial muscles, minimizing expression lines when used topically.
mechanismOfAction: Hexapeptide that inhibits SNARE complex formation, reducing acetylcholine release at neuromuscular junctions to relax facial muscles topically.

name: Copper Tripeptide-1 (Cosmetic)
description: Common cosmetic copper peptide promoting cellular renewal and skin hydration.
mechanismOfAction: Copper peptide that stimulates dermal fibroblast activity, promoting cellular renewal and collagen deposition for skin hydration and repair.

name: Decorinyl (Tripeptide-10)
description: A tetrapeptide that mimics decorin, coordinating collagen fibril organization for skin firmness.
mechanismOfAction: Decorin-mimetic peptide that coordinates collagen fibril organization and promotes uniform collagen lattice structure for skin firmness.

name: Epitalon
description: A synthetic tetrapeptide (Epithalon) that stimulates telomerase activity, extending telomere length and retarding age-related cell decay.
sideEffects: No documented adverse reactions in clinical studies
mechanismOfAction: Synthetic tetrapeptide that stimulates telomerase (hTERT) activity in somatic cells, extending telomere length and normalizing pineal melatonin production.

name: Eyeseryl (Acetyl Tetrapeptide-5)
description: A peptide designed to reduce puffiness and dark circles under the eyes via anti-edematous actions.
mechanismOfAction: Acetyl Tetrapeptide-5 that inhibits glycation of tissue proteins and reduces vascular permeability to decrease periorbital edema and dark circles.

name: FOXO4-DRI
description: A retro-inverso peptide designed to interfere with FOXO4/p53 interaction, selectively inducing apoptosis (cell death) in senescent cells.
storageInfo: Keep reconstituted solution frozen or refrigerated; highly sensitive.
mechanismOfAction: Retro-inverso peptide that disrupts FOXO4-p53 nuclear interaction in senescent cells, releasing p53 to cytoplasm to trigger selective apoptosis.
cycleRecommendation: 3 doses over 6 days, repeat every 3-6 months

name: GHK (Copper-Free Peptide)
description: The base tripeptide without copper. Promotes wound healing and collagen synthesis but with lower local stinging reactions.
mechanismOfAction: Tripeptide without copper that activates wound healing pathways and collagen synthesis, chelating endogenous copper at application site.

name: GHK-Cu
description: Copper binding tripeptide naturally found in human plasma. Stimulates collagen synthesis, blood vessel development, and skin elasticity.
storageInfo: Store reconstituted solution in refrigerator. Topical forms in cool dark place.
sideEffects: Injectable form stings. Mild skin redness (if topical)
mechanismOfAction: Copper-binding tripeptide that activates integrins, stimulates collagen I/III synthesis, promotes angiogenesis, and modulates over 4000 genes involved in tissue remodeling.

name: Leuphasyl (Pentapeptide-18)
description: A novel peptide that works synergistically with Argireline to reduce expression line depth by modulating muscle contractions.
mechanismOfAction: Pentapeptide that acts through enkephalin receptor modulation to reduce muscle contractions synergistically with Argireline.

name: Matrixyl (Palmitoyl Pentapeptide-4)
description: Topical peptide that stimulates collagen and glycosaminoglycan production to minimize facial wrinkles.
storageInfo: Store at room temperature in cosmetic creams.
mechanismOfAction: Lipopeptide that mimics collagen breakdown products, triggering fibroblasts to synthesize new collagen and glycosaminoglycans via TGF-β signaling.

name: Matrixyl 3000 (Duo Peptide)
description: Cosmetic combination of Palmitoyl Tripeptide-1 and Palmitoyl Tetrapeptide-7 to stimulate skin repair pathways.
mechanismOfAction: Combination of Palmitoyl Tripeptide-1 (collagen fragment mimic) and Palmitoyl Tetrapeptide-7 (IL-6 inhibitor) for dual anti-wrinkle action.

name: Matrixyl Synthe'6
description: Palmitoyl Tripeptide-38 which stimulates six major constituents of the skin matrix.
mechanismOfAction: Palmitoyl Tripeptide-38 that activates synthesis of six major skin matrix components: collagen I, III, IV, fibronectin, hyaluronic acid, and laminin-5.

name: Snap-8 (Acetyl Octapeptide-3)
description: An octapeptide related to Argireline that diminishes the depth of facial wrinkles caused by repetitive muscle movement.
mechanismOfAction: Octapeptide that competes with SNAP-25 in the SNARE complex, inhibiting vesicle docking and neurotransmitter release to reduce expression wrinkles.

name: Syn-Ake (Tripeptide-3)
description: A small synthetic peptide modeled from snake venom that mimics Waglerin-1, working to relax facial muscles topically.
mechanismOfAction: Synthetic tripeptide modeled from Waglerin-1 (Temple Viper venom) that reversibly blocks muscular nicotinic acetylcholine receptors.

name: Bremelanotide Acetate (Vyleesi)
description: The commercially packaged FDA-approved Bremelanotide auto-injector for premenopausal women with acquired HSDD.
typicalFrequency: As needed (do not exceed 1 dose in 24 hours)
storageInfo: Store at room temperature in packaging.
mechanismOfAction: FDA-approved MC4R agonist formulated as an auto-injector for premenopausal women with acquired hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD).

name: Gonadorelin (GnRH)
description: Synthetic gonadotropin-releasing hormone that stimulates the pituitary to release LH and FSH to support testicular volume and spermatogenesis.
mechanismOfAction: Synthetic decapeptide identical to endogenous GnRH that stimulates pituitary gonadotroph cells to release LH and FSH in a pulsatile manner.

name: Human Chorionic Gonadotropin (hCG)
description: A polypeptide hormone that mimics luteinizing hormone (LH), preventing testicular atrophy and restoring testosterone production in men.
mechanismOfAction: Glycoprotein hormone that mimics LH signaling via LH/CG receptor, stimulating Leydig cell testosterone production and preventing testicular atrophy.

name: Kisspeptin-10
description: A decapeptide that stimulates gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) secretion, regulating LH/FSH production, testosterone levels, and libido.
mechanismOfAction: Decapeptide that activates GPR54 on GnRH neurons, triggering pulsatile GnRH release and downstream LH/FSH secretion for reproductive hormone regulation.

name: Kisspeptin-54
description: A longer form of Kisspeptin that regulates reproductive function and libido, with a slightly longer biological activity than Kisspeptin-10.
mechanismOfAction: Full-length kisspeptin that activates GPR54 with longer biological activity than Kisspeptin-10, regulating the HPG axis for reproductive function.

name: Leuprolide (Low Dose)
description: Luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone analog studied at low doses for hormonal pulse restoration.
mechanismOfAction: LHRH analog that at low doses may restore pulsatile LH/FSH release, while high doses cause receptor desensitization and hormonal suppression.

name: Melanotan I (Afamelanotide)
description: An FDA-approved melanocortin agonist (Scenesse) for erythropoietic protoporphyria, used for skin tanning and libido enhancement with less nausea than Melanotan II.
mechanismOfAction: Selective MC1R agonist that stimulates eumelanin production without significant MC4R activation, providing UV-free tanning with minimal sexual side effects.
researchEvidence: Phase III Clinical Trial (Approved for EPP)

name: Melanotan II
description: A non-selective melanocortin receptor agonist that promotes skin tanning, libido enhancement, and mild appetite suppression.
mechanismOfAction: Non-selective melanocortin agonist (MC1R-MC5R) that promotes melanogenesis (tanning), sexual arousal (MC4R), and appetite suppression.

name: Oxytocin (Hormonal Peptide)
description: A nonapeptide hormone that promotes intimacy, sexual arousal, and social bonding, often administered intranasally.
storageInfo: Store nasal spray or vial in refrigerator.
mechanismOfAction: Nonapeptide hormone that binds oxytocin receptors in the brain and peripheral tissues, promoting social bonding, uterine contractions, and milk ejection.

name: PT-141 (Bremelanotide)
description: An FDA-approved melanocortin receptor agonist that acts on the nervous system to treat erectile dysfunction and hypoactive sexual desire disorder.
typicalFrequency: As needed (2-4 hours prior to activity)
storageInfo: Refrigerate reconstituted solution. Stable up to 30 days.
mechanismOfAction: Melanocortin receptor agonist (MC3R/MC4R) that acts centrally on the hypothalamus to initiate sexual arousal pathways independent of vascular mechanisms.
cycleRecommendation: As needed (max 1 dose per 24h, max 8 doses/month)

name: Triptorelin (GnRH agonist)
description: A GnRH agonist. An extremely small dose is occasionally used in post-cycle therapy (PCT) to restart natural testosterone production.
contraindications: Always contraindicated for ongoing use unless under strict clinical surveillance
mechanismOfAction: GnRH agonist that initially stimulates then desensitizes pituitary GnRH receptors, used in PCT at micro-doses for HPG axis restart.

name: Imunofan
description: A synthetic hexapeptide developed in Russia that acts as an immunomodulator, hepatoprotector, and detoxifying agent.
sideEffects: No side effects reported at physiological doses
mechanismOfAction: Synthetic hexapeptide that normalizes oxidative stress markers, activates NF-κB-mediated antioxidant enzymes, and modulates T-helper cell balance.

name: LL-37 (Antimicrobial)
description: An antimicrobial peptide naturally occurring in human cells, showing potent antibacterial, antiviral, and tissue remodeling properties.
storageInfo: Store reconstituted solution at 2-8°C. Avoid frequent freezing.
mechanismOfAction: Cathelicidin-derived antimicrobial peptide that disrupts microbial membranes, activates TLR signaling, and recruits immune cells for innate defense.

name: Rigin (Immunomodulator)
description: A synthetic peptide that mimics the immunomodulatory fragment of immunoglobulin G, helping to regulate inflammatory cytokine cascades.
mechanismOfAction: Synthetic IgG fragment mimic that regulates inflammatory cytokine cascades, modulating TNF-α and IL-1β to balance immune responses.

name: Splenopentin (SP-5)
description: A synthetic pentapeptide corresponding to the active site of the splenic hormone splenopin, regulating immune cell replication.
mechanismOfAction: Synthetic pentapeptide of splenopin active site that regulates immune cell replication via modulation of spleen-derived immunoregulatory signals.

name: Thymopentin (TP-5)
description: A synthetic pentapeptide corresponding to the active site of thymopoietin. Used to enhance immune response and support rheumatoid arthritis treatments. Also used as an immunopotentiator to stimulate antibody titers and T-cell counts.
mechanismOfAction: Synthetic pentapeptide of thymopoietin active site that induces T-cell differentiation markers (CD2, CD3) and enhances immune cell-mediated responses.
researchEvidence: Phase III Clinical Trial (Approved in some regions)

name: Thymosin Alpha-1
description: An immunomodulatory peptide that stimulates T-cell maturation and natural killer cell activity, used to support immune defense against chronic infections.
storageInfo: Store reconstituted solution in refrigerator (2-8°C). Use within 28 days.
mechanismOfAction: Immunomodulatory peptide that activates toll-like receptors (TLR2, TLR9), stimulates dendritic cell maturation, T-cell differentiation, and NK cell activity.
researchEvidence: Phase III Clinical Trial (Approved outside US)

name: Thymostimulin (TP-1)
description: Purified thymic extract containing low-molecular-weight polypeptides, studied for improving cell-mediated immunity in cancer chemotherapy patients.
mechanismOfAction: Purified thymic extract containing low-MW polypeptides that stimulate cell-mediated immunity by promoting T-cell maturation.

name: Thymovocal (Thymus fraction)
description: Peptides sourced from young bovine thymus glands used to support age-related immune deficiency and immune wellness.
mechanismOfAction: Bovine thymus-derived peptides that support age-related immune deficiency by providing thymic factors for T-cell differentiation.

name: Thymulin
description: A zinc-dependent thymic hormone peptide that regulates T-lymphocyte differentiation and function. Also studied for hair follicle regrowth and protection against skin collagen breakdown.
sideEffects: No major side effects reported at research doses
mechanismOfAction: Zinc-dependent nonapeptide hormone secreted by thymic epithelial cells that regulates T-lymphocyte differentiation, NF-κB modulation, and hair follicle cycling.

name: Tuftsin
description: A naturally occurring tetrapeptide (Thr-Lys-Pro-Arg) produced by enzymatic cleavage of IgG in the spleen. Stimulates phagocytosis and macrophage activity.
mechanismOfAction: Natural tetrapeptide from IgG heavy chain that stimulates phagocytosis, macrophage migration, and superoxide anion production for innate immunity.
